$comment: Roblox's published financial figures, as filed with the SEC. Nothing here is scraped, sampled or estimated by this site, and no figure is carried over from memory: each one was read out of the filing named in its `sourceId` on `retrievedAt`.

`origin` records how a figure came to be. `reported` means it appears in the filing exactly as stated here. `derived` means it is the result of subtracting reported figures from one another - for example a first quarter obtained from a six-month total minus the second quarter - which is exact arithmetic on published numbers but is not itself a number Roblox printed. The page labels the two differently.

Amounts are in whole US dollars, kept as strings so no figure passes through a JSON number and picks up floating-point error. Values reported in thousands are recorded to the dollar; values reported in millions are recorded with the trailing zeroes the filing implies and marked with the precision they were published at.
This is deliberately not a live feed. Roblox reports quarterly, so quarterly is the honest resolution. See docs/decision-log.md, decision D-026.

companyContext holds figures quoted verbatim from the release rather than recomputed, because each is already a rounded published figure and re-deriving it would only introduce a difference this site would then have to explain. There is deliberately no share price: a live quote needs a paid market-data feed and a third-party script, and neither belongs on a page whose whole claim is that every number is traceable to a filing.
